correctness.rationale: The Riesz Green kernel gives G(x,x)=int R(x,y)dy/T-[int int R(y,z)dydz]/(2T²). The cactus block-cut tree decomposes effective resistances into bridge interval and circular parallel-arc kernels; projecting arclength to each block adds exterior vertex masses, yielding the displayed Phi_B and J_B formulas. Bridges have strictly convex Phi, and attachment-free cycle arcs strictly concave Phi with at most one critical point. At any cycle attachment positive exterior mass produces an upward derivative jump, precluding a maximum, while bridge cut vertices admit an outgoing increasing direction; pure circle is constant. These steps prove the candidate rule. Independently recomputed the nonantipodal example K=(2341/75)/15-(4033/10)/(2*15²)=1777/1500. Finite rational source verification is illustrative rather than complete proof.
